narrative: OMX30 enters Tuesday with constructive European backdrop as DAX leads the continent. Swedish krona weakness (USD/SEK +53bps, EUR/SEK +31bps) is a tailwind for the 40% export-heavy index, particularly industrials and tech. Technicals remain supportive: the index sits at 96% of 52-week range with MACD bullish crossover, though RSI at 66.17 and stochastic K at 74.9 signal neutral-to-overbought conditions warranting caution on fresh long entries. The 90bp drop in US 10Y yield (-0.81%) is a mixed signal—positive for real estate refinancing but compressing tech valuations heading into a NASDAQ-negative session. Asian weakness and VIX uptick suggest rotation toward defensive plays over momentum.
morningBrief: OMX30 expected to open +0.4–0.5% on European strength and krona weakness supporting exporters. Key support at 3085 (lower Bollinger band), resistance at 3180 (50-MA), pivot at 3123. Watch USD/SEK stability above 9.72—breaches below 9.65 would weaken the export thesis. Industrials (Atlas Copco, Volvo B, Sandvik) lead on FX tailwinds; Banks (SEB A, Handelsbanken A, Swedbank A) consolidate on lower yields (NIM compression risk). Essity and AstraZeneca outperform on risk-off sentiment; Ericsson and Hexagon face headwinds from NASDAQ weakness and AI sell-off (chipmaker rotation). Oil down 2.94% eases input cost pressure on consumer names. Stochastic overbought state (K=74.9) and RSI neutral suggest a pullback to 50-MA possible intraday—use weakness to add to bull thesis. US Jobless Claims at 14:30 CET (soft data expected) and ongoing China concerns will dictate afternoon momentum. ADX above 18 maintains confidence, but avoid new entries above upper Bollinger band.
